Taswira · From Kanem to Bornu

46 seconds · 1920×1080 · 60 fps · silent prototype. Press Play, then use the player's full-screen button.

From Kanem to Bornu, 1376 to about 1488: the Bulala from around Lake Fitri, Mai Umar ibn Idris's move west of Lake Chad, and Ngazargamu. Dates that differ are labelled; Lake Chad is today's outline, not a period shoreline. Original Zomo artwork accompanies the map. Architectural arrangements and counts are schematic; this is an unreviewed draft.

Download the MP4 · Where each place and date comes from

Captions and transcript
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:03.500
From around Lake Fitri, to the east, came the Bulala.

2
00:00:03.500 --> 00:00:09.200
By one account they killed five of the six kings who reigned between 1376 and 1400.

3
00:00:09.200 --> 00:00:16.200
Mai Umar ibn Idris left Njimi and led the Kanembu west, to Bornu, on the far side of the lake.

4
00:00:16.200 --> 00:00:19.400
The move is dated from about 1380 to 1387.

5
00:00:19.400 --> 00:00:25.000
In Bornu the Kanembu married into the peoples already there, and from them came the Kanuri.

6
00:00:25.000 --> 00:00:27.800
For decades the court had no lasting seat.

7
00:00:27.800 --> 00:00:31.000
Then Mai Ali Gaji built Ngazargamu, between two rivers.

8
00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:36.000
Its founding is dated anywhere from about 1460 to 1488.
